title: Approximate Matrix Multiplication over Sliding Windows

problem.claim: Develop efficient approximate matrix multiplication algorithms for streaming data, particularly for computing products over the most recent columns within sliding windows.

gap.claim: Existing approximate matrix multiplication needs in practical time-sensitive streaming scenarios motivate efficient algorithms specialized to sliding windows.

contributions.claim: Two deterministic algorithms are presented for approximate matrix multiplication over sliding windows, with corresponding error guarantees.
For sparse matrices, the methods are improved in space and time cost using an approximate singular value decomposition that exploits matrix sparsity.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the two deterministic algorithms as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets are reported to validate the theoretical analysis and demonstrate the efficiency of the methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Streaming matrix multiplication is common, creating interest in efficient approximate methods.
Time-sensitive applications require multiplication over recent matrix columns rather than entire matrices, motivating sliding-window AMM.
The paper introduces two deterministic algorithms with error guarantees.
The methods are made more space- and time-efficient for sparse matrices through approximate singular value decomposition.
Synthetic and real-world experiments are reported as supporting the theoretical analysis and method efficiency.

source_observation.claim: The approach targets recent columns in streaming matrices and provides deterministic algorithms with error guarantees.

interpretation.claim: Approximation methods for streaming data can be aligned with recency requirements while retaining explicit error control.

application.claim: For time-sensitive streaming workloads, consider sliding-window computation with deterministic approximation guarantees.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the window model, guarantee form, or conditions under which the algorithms apply.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the algorithm designs or error-bound forms.
